title: These Gurus Taught Me Mortgage Fraud
summary: Real estate agent fact-checks a guru podcast: low-down-payment loans require owner occupancy, authorized-user credit hacks do not pass mortgage underwriting, stacking 3%-down rentals is fraud.

assertions.quote: If you are trying to game the system and acquire investment properties with 3 to 10% down, then you will be found very quickly.

verdicts.note: Occupancy misrepresentation on a mortgage application is federal fraud and underwriters check recent loans.

assertions.quote: the requirements are that you live in the house for at least one year as your primary residence

verdicts.note: Conventional and FHA low-down loans require owner occupancy for at least twelve months.

assertions.quote: Lenders are able to see that your boost in credit score comes from being an authorized user

verdicts.note: Scoring models and manual underwriting discount authorized-user tradelines.

assertions.quote: the difference between 3% interest rate and 4% interest rate is around $50,000 for the entirety of a 30-year loan

verdicts.note: One point of rate on a thirty-year loan compounds to tens of thousands in interest.

assertions.quote: if you didn't gas on it, they're going to send you a 4, $500,000 credit card

verdicts.note: Issuers raise limits based on usage and payment history, and cut dormant lines.

assertions.quote: your debt to income will be insane if you go out and buy 10 properties with $20,000 down, and no one will lend to you

verdicts.note: Hard-money lenders require larger equity and lenders cap debt-to-income.

assertions.quote: if they don't get back into you in a certain time, they legally have to remove this stuff off your credit

verdicts.note: The Fair Credit Reporting Act requires removal of items not verified within thirty days.

assertions.quote: it's way easier to be a fake guru promoting get-rich-easy schemes than it is to be someone who's transparent

verdicts.note: Describes a marketing omission, not a measurable outcome.
